newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine public sector deficit at 2.5 bln pesos.
newsitem.headline: Philippine public sector deficit at 2.5 bln pesos.

text.p: The Philippine government said on Thursday its consolidated public sector deficit reached about 2.5 billion pesos as of December 10, 1996.
Budget Secretary Salvador Enriquez said in a statement that the government is however likely to be able to balance the books for the year by cutting down on expenditures in the next two weeks.

"To ensure the attainment of the target balanced consolidated public sector fiscal posititon for 1996, the Development Budget Coordination Committee (DBCC) has decided to rein in disbursements," Enriquez said. The public sector deficit includes that of the national government, government corporations, the central bank and others.

The budget chief traced the public sector deficit to a shortfall in revenues, especially in non-tax revenue collections. Total reveneues had reached 413.2 billion pesos so far this year against a full-year target of 431.3 billion, he said.
Non-tax revenues amounted to only 42.4 billion pesos as of December 10, 1996 compared to a full-year target of 60.9 billion pesos.
Of the non-tax revenues, privatisation proceeds amounted to only 4.4 billion pesos, or 17.1 billion pesos less than the 1996 target of 21.5 billion pesos.
Manila has deferred to 1997 the privatisation of certain state-owned assetrs scheduled for this year. They include Manila Electric Co shares and real estate assets.
Enriquez said the move to control the deficit was aimed at minimising government borrowings and containing the rise in inflation and interest rates.
